summary: A SIXTH press-lane gap of the identical class to the three DB-019 closed, found while authoring them and NOT closed, because DB-019's working set is three literal migration filenames. `public.press_release_shares` is created ONLY by the ARCHIVED supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20/20260717221000_press_release_shares.sql. It is absent from the 320-file active chain AND absent from lib/database.types.ts, and it has live consumers. THE CONSEQUENCE IS A HARD 403, NOT A COSMETIC ONE: lib/press/press-release-access.ts:63-70 `canAccessPressRelease` returns `{ allowed: false }` for every NON-owner, so app/api/press/releases/[id]/pdf/route.ts:33 403s every shared recipient, and `recordPressReleaseDownload` (:74-83) has no table to update. The press-release SHARE FEATURE does not work at all today, and DB-019's 20260927130000 does not change that — it restores the `format`/`embargo_until`/`boilerplate` columns that `getPressReleaseById` reads, so the function gets FURTHER before it returns false. A press lane that tests only the owner path will see the restore work and conclude the feature works. The column contract is fully derivable from the single consumer (id, press_post_id, recipient_user_id, downloaded_at, created_at) and the archive is the source, so this is a small, well-specified migration for whoever owns the press lane. It is routed rather than authored because adding a sixth relation to a file named news_press_schema_gaps would be scope expansion into the press lane's authorization surface, and because the SHARE authorization model — who may receive a press release, whether a share is revocable, whether an embargo blocks a shared recipient — is a product decision the database lane must not make unilaterally.

completed: Established by scoped search, NOT by a bare column-name grep: `rg -l press_release_shares --glob '!node_modules'` returns 4 live code/test/doc consumers and exactly ONE migration hit, and that migration is in supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20/, which is not in the active chain. `python3` over lib/database.types.ts confirms the relation is not declared in the contract either. The scoped-search discipline is the one DB-008 recorded after `marketplace_storefronts.status` was reported with 2,158 consumers citing files that read no marketplace table.

Read the single consumer end to end and derived the contract from it rather than from the archive alone: `canAccessPressRelease` reads `press_post_id` and `recipient_user_id` from the share and updates `downloaded_at`; `getPressReleaseById` uses `.maybeSingle()` on `(id)`, so the share lookup's own uniqueness is `(press_post_id, recipient_user_id)` — a duplicate share would make `maybeSingle()` return PGRST116 and deny a legitimate recipient.

Confirmed this is the SAME class as the three gaps DB-019 closed and the same class the discover lane's guard test would catch: a live select of a relation that exists nowhere, producing zero diagnostics because lib/press/press-release-access.ts reaches Supabase through the un-generic `SupabaseClient`.

Confirmed DB-019's own migration does not make it worse and does not fix it: 20260927130000_news_press_schema_gaps.sql restores the five columns `getPressReleaseById` selects, so the function now completes its read and reaches the share lookup instead of failing earlier.
next_steps: Supply the share authorization contract before any migration is authored, because it decides the RLS: is a share row readable by the recipient, by the sharer, by both, or by neither once downloaded? Is a share revocable (a `revoked_at` column) or is a delete the only revocation? Does `embargo_until` on the parent `artist_blog_posts` row block a SHARED recipient, or only the public page? The last question is currently unanswerable from the code, because the PDF route never compares `embargo_until` to `now()` at all — see HF-DB-019-PRESS-EMBARGO-AND-BOILERPLATE-READ-SCOPE.

Author the table additively as a NEW migration at a version after 20260927130200, porting the archived 20260717221000 forward rather than moving or editing the archive, with `create table if not exists`, RLS enabled AND forced, own-side-and-recipient-side policies only, an explicit unique constraint on `(press_post_id, recipient_user_id)` for the `maybeSingle()` reason above, `references auth.users(id) on delete cascade` on the recipient so account deletion erases the share, and a planned manifest in the same shape as DB-019's three.

Extend the `__tests__/news/news-feed-schema-drift.test.ts` guard OR add the press equivalent so this class cannot recur in the press lane. The news guard already generalises the lesson — 'a column-level guard cannot be replaced by a diagnostic count, because the count is a lower bound on drift, never an upper bound' — and it is scoped to `lib/news/**` only, so `lib/press/**` is currently unguarded.

After the apply, CP-016 regeneration makes lib/database.types.ts declare the table; until then the type error is the only machine-readable evidence it is missing, and that error is why this gap is cheap to find once someone looks for it.
blockers: The database lane did not author this migration and will not: DB-019's working set is three literal filenames (20260927130000, 20260927130100, 20260927130200) and its AC-1 names five items. Adding a sixth relation to a file named `news_press_schema_gaps` would be silent scope expansion into the press lane's authorization surface. Control: no migration filename outside DB-019's list was created, and the record says so.

The share AUTHORIZATION model is a product decision, not a schema decision, and the archive cannot supply it — the archived migration predates any RLS on the table, so porting it verbatim would create a share table with no policy at all, which for a table holding 'who received this press release' is a disclosure surface rather than a neutral one. The database lane will not invent the answer.

The embargo question is unresolved and blocks a correct RLS: if `embargo_until` is meant to gate distribution, then a shared recipient's access is a function of a column on a DIFFERENT table, and expressing that in a policy is a decision with disclosure consequences. Routed jointly rather than answered here.

No hosted or credentialed verification was performed and none is claimed. The 403 conclusion is derived from reading `canAccessPressRelease` and the PDF route's `if (!access.allowed || !access.release) return 403` — it is a code-path derivation, not an observed request. Release/QA should confirm by exercising a non-owner share against a deployed environment.
The archive is evidence and was not moved, edited or applied. `supabase db reset` was not run and no migration was applied to any environment (CP-051).
